population: 165M applicants; 15M candidates; 1.2M hires; Gem customers; Jun 2021-May 2025
key_result: 8% advance past screening; 0.5% ultimately hired; referrals convert 11x inbound; direct sourcing yields 11% of hires from 2.6% of applications
limits: not FAANG-specific; customer-base selection; no interview-prep treatment

population: Ashby customer hiring processes; role cuts reported through Q1 2026
key_result: applications per hire above 300 throughout 2025; technical roles 17.6 interviews per hire; engineering 17.9
limits: not FAANG-specific; no candidate preparation treatment

population: about 10,000 real anonymous interviews; preselected strong mock performers; 2016-2022
key_result: 46% of offer recipients lacked top school or top company; some had prior resume-stage rejection at same employer; thousands placed
causal_strength: observational platform experiment with changed resume visibility
limits: commercial self-report; average hire 10 YOE; preselected strong interviewers; no ordinary-entry treatment

population: platform users; public article says platform had close to 100K interviews
key_result: at least five practice interviews associated with almost 2x pass likelihood
limits: public article does not expose full denominator/model; selection and treatment confounding

population: almost 700 surveyed platform users with LeetCode + LinkedIn + interview data
key_result: total problems correlation about 0.27 with interview performance and 0.17 with ever-FAANG; authors explicitly caution correlation is not causation
limits: platform-user selection; retrospective; confounding; ever-FAANG is not a post-treatment offer measure

population: 131 candidates actively preparing for software-engineering technical interviews
key_result: communication rehearsal and practice with others significantly associated with perceived preparedness; more weekly study hours and LeetCode problems/day were not
limits: perceived preparedness rather than hiring; self-report; no randomized treatment

population: 3,526 intervention population; 512 survey responses; competitive public-university DSA students
measured_outcome: recalled effect on employment and qualitative employment outcomes
key_result: among 363 recallers: 33% agree/strongly agree activities helped secure employment, 49% neutral, 18% disagree; 7/347 qualitative respondents explicitly credited activities with interview/internship success
limits: 15% response rate; self-report; no randomized employment comparison; already in computing program
